## Question 7 Prep - Multi-Page Scraping

```{r one_webpage}
isa_url = "https://bulletin.miamioh.edu/courses-instruction/isa"
# holds the address
# has to be in quotes since URLs are text

isa_page = rvest::read_html(isa_url)
    # readh_html() retrieves/parses the HTML - html specific
    # isa_page stores the parsed page

class(isa_page) # output IDing an HTML document

isa_titles = isa_page |>
  rvest::html_elements("p.courseblocktitle") |>
    #searches an HTML document for elements matching a CSS selector
    # p = HTML para element, . = indicates a CSS class, # courseblocktitle is the name of the class
    # intepret as "find every paragraph with class courseblocktitle
  rvest::html_text2()
    # extracts HTML into ordinary text that R can use
    # different from html_attr("href") - extracts an HTML attribute

head(isa_titles) # displayed first 6 course titles
length(isa_titles) # confirmed you extracted 50 course titles
```

```{r multiple departments}
dept_abbrv = c("acc", "bus", "isa", "mkt")
  # c() combines values into a vector (dept_abbrv)
  # "quotation marks" indicate character strings

courses_df = data.frame() # creates an empty data frame

for (abbrv in dept_abbrv) { # begin code to be repeated
  # for begins a loop, in = iterate through each value in vector
  
  bulletin_url = paste0(  # combines text without adding separators
  "https://bulletin.miamioh.edu/courses-instruction/",
  abbrv,
  "/"
)
  webpage = rvest::read_html(bulletin_url)
  
  titles = webpage |>
    rvest::html_elements("p.courseblocktitle") |>
    rvest::html_text2()
  
  df = data.frame( # creates a data frame for the current dept
      department = abbrv,
      title = titles
  )
  
  courses_df = rbind(courses_df, df)
    # rbind = row bind - combines data frames vertically
}

nrow(courses_df) # total number of scraped course titles

dplyr::count(courses_df, department)
  # one row for each dept, its # of scraped courses
head(courses_df)
```

```{r 7_final_practice}
dept_abbrv = c("acc", "bus", "isa", "mkt")
  # c() combines values into a vector (dept_abbrv)
courses_df = data.frame() # creates an empty data frame

for (abbrv in dept_abbrv) { # begin code to be repeated
  # for begins a loop, in = iterate through each value in vector
  bulletin_url = paste0(
  "https://bulletin.miamioh.edu/courses-instruction/",
  abbrv,
  "/")

webpage = rvest::read_html(bulletin_url)

  titles = webpage |>
    rvest::html_elements("p.courseblocktitle") |>
    # remember to add the pipe
    rvest::html_text2()
  
  descs = webpage |>
    rvest::html_elements("p.courseblockdesc") |>
    rvest::html_text2()

  print(c(abbrv, length(titles), length(descs)))

  df = data.frame(
    department = abbrv,
    title = titles,
    description = descs
  )
  
  courses_df = rbind(courses_df, df)
    # rbind = row bind - combines data frames vertically
}

nrow(courses_df) # total number of scraped course titles
ncol(courses_df)
dplyr::count(courses_df, department)
  # one row for each dept, its # of scraped courses
head(courses_df, 3)
```


## Question 6 Practice - Debugging AI-Written API requests

```{r api_practice}
crashes = httr2::request(
  "https://data.cincinnati-oh.gov/resource/rvmt-pkmq.json"
) |> # creates request to API endpoint
  httr2::req_url_query("$limit" = 5) |> # adds parameters to URL
  httr2::req_perform() |> # sends request to the server
    # actually communicates with the server
  httr2::resp_body_string() |> # extracts response body as text
  jsonlite::fromJSON() # parses JSON into an R object

dplyr::glimpse(crashes) # insepcts the returned data

class(crashes)
nrow(crashes)
names(crashes)
head(crashes)
```

```{r crash_example}
recent_crashes = httr2::request(
  "https://data.cincinnati-oh.gov/resource/rvmt-pkmq.json"
) |>
  httr2::req_url_query(
    "$select" = "crashdate,community_council_neighborhood,crashseverity",
    "$where" = "crashdate IS NOT NULL",
    "$order" = "crashdate DESC",
    "$limit" = 5
  ) |>
  httr2::req_perform() |>
  httr2::resp_body_string() |>
  jsonlite::fromJSON()

recent_crashes

names(recent_crashes)
```

```{r authentication}

ohio_jobs = httr2::request(
  "https://api.stlouisfed.org/fred/series/observations"
) |>
  httr2::req_url_query(
    series_id = "IHLIDXUSOH",
    api_key = Sys.getenv("FRED_API_KEY"),
    file_type = "json"
) |>
  httr2::req_perform() |>
  httr2::resp_body_string() |>
  jsonlite::fromJSON()

names(ohio_jobs)
```


## Question 4: Nested JSON

```{r nested_json_practice}
job = list(
  company = "Google",
  location = "Ohio",
  salary = list(minimum = 85000, maximum = 125000
  ),
  skills = c ("R", "SQL", "Excel")) # character vector, not a nested list
  
str(job) # shows how the object is organized, including nested elements

names(job) # reveals names of outer elements
names(job$salary) # reveals names of elements within salary

job[3][2] # returns NULL
job$skills[3] # returns "Excel"

#Correct Code
job[[3]][[2]]
job$salary$maximum
job$skills[[2]]
```

```{r reading_real_json}
campus = jsonlite::fromJSON( # reads/parses JSON into R object
  "https://isa401-find-your-seat.vercel.app/campus.json"
)

class(campus) # identifies the object type
names(campus) # displays named elements
str(campus, max.level = 2) # shows the structure, including nested elements
# max.level = 2 limits how many lnested levels str() displays

fsb = campus$Farmer # or campus[[5]]

names(fsb)
str(fsb, max.level = 2)

fsb[[8]]

# According to the campus JSON file, how many sections are on the second floor of the Farmer School of Business?
#AI Answer A
campus["Farmer"][[8]]$`2`$sections # starts with a one-element list, therefore is wrong (tries to retrieve the 8th element)

#AI Answer B
campus$Farmer[[8]]$`2`$sections


second_floor = campus$Farmer[[8]]$`2`

names(second_floor)
str(second_floor, max.level = 1)

rooms = second_floor[[3]]

class(rooms)
dim(rooms)
names(rooms)
head(rooms)

# recall, rooms[6,2] means row 6, column 2
# row[6, "isa_sections"] means row 6, column isa_sections

names(campus)
names(fsb)
campus["Farmer"][[8]]$`2`$sections
campus$Farmer[[8]]$`2`$sections


second_floor = campus$Farmer[[8]]$`2`
rooms = second_floor[[3]]

class(rooms)
dim(rooms)
names(rooms)
rooms[6, "isa_sections"]
```


# Question 3 - Predict R Output

```{r tricky_examples}
x = c(4, 8, 12, 16)
names(x) = c("A", "B", "C", "D")
y = c(TRUE, FALSE, TRUE, FALSE)

x[y] # I think it will result in true
  # resulted in A / 4, C / 12 , so I guess it's all X that y returns true
sum(y) # counts all, I think it counts 4
  # counted 2, so it must be just the true ones
typeof(x) # I think it will be double
  # I was right
x[2:3] # I think it returns 8,12
  # It returned it with their names B / 8, C / 12


a = c(2, 4, 6, 8)
b = c(10,20)
c = c(1, "2", 3)

a + b # I think this will return the sum of everything (50)
  # no, it added the individuals, keeping the list
typeof(c) # it will be a character
  # i was right, "2" throws it off
c[2] # just "2"?
  # yeah I was right
c[2] == 2 # no because its text/character
  # I was wrong, TRUE
```


# Question 1 - Evaluating AI Claims about a Data File

```{r question 1}
# important skills:
  # 1) checking actual # of rows, columns
  # 2) IDing column names and data types
  # 3) distinguishing character values from numbers
  # 4) evaluating whether AI accurately describes a dataset

# 4 variables, 4 observations
employees = data.frame(
  name = c("Anna", "Ben", "Chris", "Diana"),
  department = c("Finance", "Marketing", "Finance", "Operations"),
  salary = c("75000", "82000", "90000", "68000"),
  remote = c(TRUE, FALSE, TRUE, FALSE)
)

dplyr::glimpse(employees)
# the salaries are all characters, we probably want to switch them over to doubles
mean(employees$remote) # = 0.5, options are 0 or 1

# to calculate the avg salary:
mean(as.numeric(employees$salary))

nrow(employees)
ncol(employees)

class(employees)
typeof(employees$salary)
typeof(employees$remote)

mean(employees$salary)
mean(employees$remote)
```


# Questions 8/9 - Tidy vs Technically Correct Data

```{r tidy_technically_correct}
crashes = data.frame(
  date = c("29 Jan 2025", "17 Feb 2025", "12 Jun 2025"),
  location_operator = c(
    "Washington DC / American Eagle",
    "Toronto / Delta Connection",
    "Ahmedabad / Air India"
  ),
  fatalities = c("67/67(0)", "0/80(0)", "241/242(19)")
)

dplyr::glimpse(crashes)

# Question 8: is this data tidy?
  # 3 rules:
      # 1) each variable is a column
      # 2) each observation is a row
      # 3) each value occupies its own cell
  # Answer: the dataset is not tidy, as location_operator and fatalities columns have multiple variables

# Question 9: is this dataset technically correct?
  # in terms of having appropriate column names and types?
  typeof(crashes$date)
  # Answer: no, date is a character, should be date, fatalities should be doubles - they should be separated and converted
```

# Question 10 - Evaluating AI Answer about dplyr

```{r question_10}
select() # which columns are kept
filter() # which rows are kept
mutate() # adds or modifies columns
group_by() # defines groups for subsequent operations
summarise() # produces summary values, often one row per group
arrange() # changes row order
count() # counts observations by category

# consider this data set
jobs = data.frame(
  company = c("ABC", "XYZ", "ABC", "DEF"),
  state = c("OH", "OH", "KY", "OH"),
  remote = c(1, 0, 1, 1)
)

# following code
jobs |>
  dplyr::filter(state == "OH") |> # keeps only OHio jobs
  dplyr::group_by(company) |> # organizes by company
  dplyr::summarise(remote_share = mean(remote))
    # one row per company, mean(remote) calculates proportion of jobs with remote = 1 (they are all 100% or 0%)
```

# Some Helpers on Q1, Q8-10

```{r helpers}
# Inspect a data frame
class(df)
dim(df)
names(df)
str(df)
dplyr::glimpse(df)

# Check particular variables
typeof(df$column_name)
class(df$column_name)

# Examine values
head(df)
unique(df$column_name)

# Count categories
dplyr::count(df, column_name)

# Check for missing values
sum(is.na(df$column_name))
```


# Question 11 - fixing AI-written ellmer code

```{r}
# important functions
ellmer::chat_openai() # creates the AI client
chat$chat_structured() # requests structured info from text
ellmer::type_object() # defines the fields to extract
ellmer::type_string() # specifies a text field
ellmer::type_integer() # specifies an integer field
ellmer::type_number() # specifies a numeric field (can have decimals)

chat = ellmer::chat_openai( # set up the client
  model = "gpt-5.6-luna",
  params = ellmer::params(
    reasoning_effort = "none"
  )
)
 # extract info from the source text
course_info = chat$chat_structured(
  isa125_text,
  type = ellmer::type_object(  # what fields should appear?
    name = ellmer::type_string( # begin specifying types
      "Name of the course"
    ),
    credit_hours = ellmer::type_integer(
      "Number of credit hours"
    ),
    prereqs = ellmer::type_string(
      "Prerequisites for the course",
      required = FALSE
    )
  )
)

## LLM extractions don't guarantee factual accuracy

```
